Welcome
Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School is a deeply inclusive and welcoming school, driven by a vision that ensures every child and adult can flourish.
Our dedicated staff team is committed to nurturing the whole child, providing an inspiring environment where spiritual and academic growth go hand-in-hand. We strive to offer a transformative learning experience rooted in dignity and respect, and we hope this website captures the community and joy that defines our school family.
If you would like to find out more about Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School please contact the school office 01435 862941.
School Values
Cross in Hand Church of England Primary School has established Respect, Community, Kindness, and Perseverance as its four core Christian values to provide a moral and spiritual compass that guides every aspect of school life.
By weaving these specific values into the curriculum and daily interactions, the school provides practical, life-enhancing force that drives both academic achievement and personal wellbeing.
Thrive
Thrive Approach is a tangible expression of "Dignity and Respect," as it treats each child as a unique individual made in the image of God, providing bespoke support. It bridges the gap between the school's theological values and practical mental health support.

Clubs
At Cross in Hand we aim to provide a range of clubs during term time. Whilst some may run throughout the year, others may only run for a specified time. We would encourage all pupils to participate and try the clubs on offer. Most clubs offered are organised by outside agencies while some teachers have their own areas of expertise and interest and offer additional opportunities for pupils in these areas.
When the children join a club, we expect commitment from them and if they cannot attend, it is their responsibility to notify the teacher running the club. If a child decides they do not want to continue with a club, they should also tell the teacher to allow that space to be taken by another child as there is often a waiting list. We expect the same high standards of behaviour in clubs as we do in school and so we make pupils aware that if their behaviour falls short of this, they may lose their space and their parents will be notified.
A letter about clubs on offer is sent out at the start of each term.

Yoto Project
Reading sits at the heart of every child’s learning journey. Strong reading skills open the door to the full curriculum, building confidence, curiosity, and a lifelong love of learning. From the earliest years, we prioritise creating joyful, meaningful reading experiences for all our pupils.
Our Yoto Project brings this vision to life by pairing older and younger children through the magic of storytelling. Older pupils record captivating audio versions of favourite books, which are then turned into bespoke Yoto cards. Younger children listen to these recordings while following along in their own copies, strengthening both comprehension and enthusiasm for reading.
To ensure everyone in Reception, Year 1 & Year 2 can take part, Yoto players and book sets rotate around the children. This simple but powerful routine helps foster connection, independence, and a shared love of stories throughout our school community.
Reception, Year 1 & Year 2
Children will take it in turn to take home the Yoto player and the books and they will be able to listen to older children reading their favourite stories as the follow along in the books.
Thanks to the Friends of Cross in Hand School for funding this project.

Relationships, Sex and Health Education
RSHE is taught across the school using a scheme called Jigsaw: The Mindful Approach to RSHE. Jigsaw teaches children to become aware of their thoughts and feelings, as they happen, helping them to concentrate, focus and regulate their emotional states.
It covers the following 'puzzles' or units of work: Being Me in My World, Celebrating Difference, Dreams & Goals, Healthy Me, Relationships and Changing Me. This last ‘puzzle’ is where we teach our Sex and Relationships Education (SRE).
